# HTTP API routes

<!-- GENERATED by `just api-docs` from crates/kb-server/src/router.rs.
     Do not edit by hand; `just api-docs-check` fails CI when stale. -->

The complete route table, extracted from the router declaration. The narrative API guide (auth, shapes, examples) lives in [docs/http-api.md](http-api.md); generated request/response types live in [web/src/api/generated/](../web/src/api/generated/).

Everything below is served from the `/api` tree (bearer-auth with loopback bypass). Three surfaces sit outside it: the top-level fallback (`<id>.artifacts.<suffix>` hosts dispatch to the sandboxed artifact server, anything else serves the SPA shell); an unauthenticated `GET /healthz` liveness probe (`{status, daemon, uptime_secs, kbs}`) mounted on the top-level router so it bypasses bearer-auth + rate-limiting; and `POST /capture` (U2, v0.25 quick capture) — the Web Share Target action, which the browser posts to bare `/capture` (no `/api` prefix). Despite living outside the nest, `/capture` carries the SAME bearer-auth + loopback bypass as the `/api` tree via an explicit `route_layer` in router.rs; see `routes::capture` for the shared handler core with `POST /api/kb/{kb}/capture` below.
